name: Kopfulme in der Beerlage

location.address: Beerlage, Bauerschaft of Billerbeck (Kreis Coesfeld), by the Steinfurter Aa, Landschaftsplan Baumberge-Nord

access: Free. Naturdenkmal (Kreis Coesfeld, ND BI 02) beside a signed foot path, public ground; the elm stands at the Steinfurter Aa. Register: 'oeffentlich zugaenglich'.
transport: About 5 km from Billerbeck station (RB63 from Muenster, ~30 min); no timetable verified for the last stretch, a bike or car is the realistic way.
verify_notes:
- Baumkunde register 3375, Baumlaeufer/Klaus Heinemann: register coordinate N52 01.9216 E7 25.1601 = 52.03203, 7.41934. OSM has a natural=tree node 1 m from it (52.03204, 7.41949) and a highway=path with foot=designated passing at 52.03201, 7.41946 (compacted surface): pin on the trunk, path to it.
- Alive: register 'vital', last visit 22.11.2025, habit photos dated 1/2026 on the register page. Hollow short trunk, remains of a pasture fence grown into the bark; deep-set crown, register notes crown reduction needed.
- Pollarded (Kopfulme = head-pollard) white elm, completely hollow with an opening; Naturdenkmal Kreis Coesfeld 'ND Kreis Coesfeld BI 02 1 Flatterulme an der Steinfurter Aa', Landschaftsplan Baumberge-Nord, 2.3.02.
- Girth: register 5.56 m measured 16.03.2020 (height 12.0 m); na-tour-denkmal (2011 piece, fetched earlier into lead) gave 5.34 m / 12.4 m / planted c.1650 +-70. Both kept; girth_cm uses the newer measurement. Age: register 300, source c.375 (planted c.1650): hold as 'roughly 350 years'.
- Recommended by the register's moderator Wolfgang Schuermann as his favourite tree.
- Twin: Baumkunde 371 'Flatter-Ulme in der Bauerschaft Beerlage bei Temming' (4.5 m, 52.01896 7.42146) is a different elm, register says Privatgelaende; not delivered.

story:
You can stand inside this elm. The trunk of the Kopfulme in der Beerlage is hollow all the way through, with an opening you can step into, and the tree is still alive around you.

Kopfulme means head-pollard elm. For generations this European white elm was cut back to a stubby head, the old way of taking wood from a tree without felling it, and that is why it grew short and wide rather than tall: 5.56 metres round when it was last measured in 2020, and only about twelve metres high. The bark has swallowed the remains of an old pasture fence, so the tree carries its working life on its skin.

How old it is depends on the source. The tree register that follows it says about 300 years. A 2011 profile put its planting near 1650, give or take seventy years, which, if that date holds, puts it in the ground within a lifetime of the Thirty Years' War. Roughly 350 is the honest middle, and the band is wide on purpose.

It stands beside a signed footpath on the Steinfurter Aa, outside Billerbeck, protected as a natural monument by the Coesfeld district. The crown sits low and needs cutting back again, which for a pollard is less a threat than a return to habit. One of the people who keeps a German tree register calls it his favourite tree of all. Step inside and you will understand him.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the short, completely hollow trunk with an opening you can step into, 5.56 metres round. It stands right beside the signed footpath along the Steinfurter Aa in the Beerlage.

name: Dicke Linde Asbeck

location.address: Lindenweg / Auf der Horst, Asbeck, Legden (Kreis Borken)

access: Free. Stands on the edge of the village at Lindenweg, a paved living street; Naturdenkmal, open to anyone.
transport: Asbeck is in Legden, about 13 km west of Billerbeck; no rail. Bus links not verified, car or bike realistic.
verify_notes:
- Baumkunde register 38: Sommer-Linde, 500 years, girth 10.47 m measured 30.09.2022, height 18 m, last visit 30.09.2022, 'vital'. Also called Gespaltene Linde, Gerichtslinde, Tanzlinde. Wikipedia (Asbeck) citing the municipality of Legden says 'about 600 years old, vital Sommerlinde with split trunk'. Sources differ 500 vs 600: age_min 500, age_max 600.
- Split trunk with a big hollow from a lightning strike; crown held by wire ropes and the trunk by steel rods since the 1980s. Said to have once carried a plank floor on which the Lords of Asbeck held feasts, and to have been the seat of a free court (Freigericht); both legend-level claims per Baumkunde, not independently sourced.
- A Bildstock showing Veronica with the veil stands under the tree (Wikipedia/legden.de); OSM has a wayside_shrine node there.
- Pin: OSM node natural=tree, denotation=natural_monument, species Tilia platyphyllos at 52.05611, 7.14978; register coordinate 52.05613, 7.14967 (8 m from Commons-geotagged photos). Confirmed.
- Alive: Commons photo 2014-04, register visit 09/2022 with photographer set from 2021-2022. Photo exists on Commons (check licence at file page before use).
- Girth is of a split, possibly fused trunk, not a single bole: say so in the story. By far the thickest tree found around Billerbeck.

story:
The Dicke Linde of Asbeck measures 10.47 metres round, and part of the reason is that it is no longer one trunk. Lightning split this large-leaved lime and left a big hollow in it. What stands now is a split trunk, possibly two stems grown together, so the figure measures all of it rather than a single bole. Either way it is the thickest tree on this page by a wide margin.

Since the 1980s steel rods have held the trunk together and wire ropes have held up the crown, which still reaches about eighteen metres. The village has more than one name for it: the split lime, the court lime, the dance lime. Those names carry the stories. One says the Lords of Asbeck once laid a plank floor in its branches and held feasts up there; another says a free court sat beneath it. Both are tradition rather than record, and nobody has found the paperwork.

Its age is disputed by about a century. The tree register that measured it in 2022 says around 500 years. The municipality of Legden says about 600. Take the range.

A small wayside shrine showing Veronica with her veil stands under the tree, at the edge of the village on Lindenweg, a quiet residential street. Asbeck is in Legden, in the west of the Münsterland, with no railway; come by bike or car.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the split, hollow trunk held together with steel rods and the wire ropes in its crown. It stands at the edge of Asbeck on Lindenweg, with a small wayside shrine underneath.

best_time.label: June, when the old lime flowers and the street smells of it

name: Krüsellinde

location.address: Alter Muensterweg (40 m NW of house no. 47), Altenberge (Kreis Steinfurt)

access: Free. In the Kruesel residential area on Alter Muensterweg with paved foot paths around it and a wayside shrine beside it; Naturdenkmal on public ground.
transport: Altenberge is about 13 km east-north-east of Billerbeck, no rail; bus links not verified, car or bike realistic.
verify_notes:
- Official: Naturdenkmal I.A 1 'Kruesellinde, 40 m NW Haus Nr. 47, Alter Muensterweg' in the Kreis Steinfurt Landschaftsplan list (de.wikipedia Liste der Naturdenkmale im Kreis Steinfurt). Wappenbaum (coat-of-arms tree) of Altenberge; Altenberge Wikipedia says old Femgerichte (vehmic courts) were held here and rope and sword still lie under the tree as symbols; Baumkunde adds a court table (Richttisch) there.

- The fungus on the trunk is a vitality caveat, say so.

story:
Altenberge put this lime on its coat of arms. The Krüsellinde is the village's heraldic tree, a large-leaved lime standing beside a wayside chapel on the Alter Münsterweg, the old road toward Münster, in what is now a residential quarter.

The spot is older in the record than the tree. Altenberge's own history says vehmic courts, the secretive Westphalian tribunals, were once held here, and that a rope and a sword still lie under the lime as symbols of that justice. The tree register adds a court table. The lime itself the register puts at about 280 years, so treat the courts and the tree as two facts about one place rather than as one story.

It is not a giant: 4.19 metres round in 2024 and about eighteen metres tall. What makes it worth looking at is the way the trunk breaks apart at around six metres into a crowd of separate stems, each one heading up on its own.

There is a caveat, and the register says it plainly. A tinder fungus is growing on the trunk. The tree was recorded as vital in October 2024, but this fungus feeds on wood, and a lime carrying it is a lime to visit sooner rather than later. If you have been recently and noticed a change, tell us.

Altenberge has no railway; a bike or a car is the realistic way out from Münster.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk that splits into many separate stems at about six metres, with a tinder fungus on the bark. It stands beside the wayside chapel on Alter Münsterweg, 40 metres north-west of house no. 47.

best_time.label: June, when the lime flowers above the wayside chapel

name: Heidenbaum

location.address: Am Heidenbaum / Darfelder Strasse (L 555), Laer (Kreis Steinfurt)

access: Free. Stands on a small hill beside the public street Am Heidenbaum near the village edge, with the Heidenkreuz stone cross and a signboard; no entry needed.
transport: Laer is about 9 km north-north-east of Billerbeck; no rail; bus links not verified, car or bike realistic.
verify_notes:
- Gerichtslinde (court lime) of the old Freigrafschaft Laer ('thor Lair thon synen Lynden', Freigericht zu den Sieben Linden); the 'Heidenkruess' sandstone cross (Baumberger Sandstein) stands under it and is said to recall Christianisation by the two Ewalds. Hill first used as court and burial place. (de.wikipedia Laer, citing Tibus 1867 and a local history; Baumkunde.)
- What is standing is a reduced remnant: Baumkunde 'Reduzierter Stamm vom Restbaum, im Boden sind noch Andeutungen der ehemaligen Groesse des Baumes zu sehen'. Girth 4.06 m (2016), height only 10 m. Age 'over 500' from Wikipedia and 500 in the register: legend-level, not measured; flagged for that and because the remnant is small.
- Alive: register 'vital', last visit 09.07.2026 (page updated 13.07.2026).
- Pin: OSM node name=Heidenbaum natural=tree genus Tilia at 52.05285, 7.34851, with Heidenkreuz node 4 m away; register coord 52.05279, 7.34849. Confirmed.
- Species: register says Sommer-Linde; OSM only genus Tilia. Species from one source.

story:
What stands at the Heidenbaum today is the remnant of a court tree, and the ground still shows how big it once was. The tree register describes a reduced trunk left from the old lime, with traces of its former size visible in the soil around it. The survivor is 4.06 metres round and only about ten metres tall, small for a tree with this much history attached.

The history is the reason to come. This was the court lime of the old free county of Laer, whose court met "thor Lair thon synen Lynden", at Laer by its limes. The little hill it stands on served as a court and a burial place. Beneath the tree stands the Heidenkreuz, a cross of local Baumberge sandstone, said to recall the conversion of the region by the two Ewalds, the missionary brothers of the seventh century.

How much of that this particular tree has seen is the open question. The register says about 500 years and Laer's encyclopedia entry says over 500, but nobody has measured it, and a figure that round is closer to tradition than to dendrology. The register names it a large-leaved lime; no second source confirms the species.

It stands on public ground beside the street Am Heidenbaum at the edge of Laer, with a signboard explaining the site. If you know more about how old it really is, tell us.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the short, cut-back lime trunk with the Heidenkreuz sandstone cross standing directly beneath it. It stands on a small hill beside the street Am Heidenbaum, by a signboard.
